subject: general
question: When performing a one way analysis of variance, which statistical test is used?
solution:
The correct answer is** F test**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** One Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA):

__
 
• F test is used in a one way analysis of variance to compare the variances between groups. 
 
• It helps in determining if there are any statistically significant differences between the means of three or more independent groups.
 
• **The F statistic is calculated as the ratio of the variance between the group means to the variance within the groups.**
 
• A larger F value indicates a greater degree of difference between the group means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Other Statistical Tests:

__
 
• z test: Used to determine if there is a significant difference between sample and population means or between two sample means. Not suitable for comparing more than two groups.
 
• χ2 test: Used to assess the association between categorical variables. Not used for comparing means.
 
• t test: Used to compare the means of two groups. Not suitable for comparing more than two groups.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__** As per the official answer key the correct answer is Χ2 test but after verifying the question again and again it is found that the correct answer should be F test. So we have explained the correct answer accordingly.
